subject: Physics
prompt: In some state of matter the molecules are widely separated and can move almost freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?
options: A gas
A solid
A liquid
A fluid
A solid or liquid
explanation_steps: Molecules widely separated and free to move in any direction characterizes a gas.

subject: Physics
prompt: The two main branches of physical sciences are
options: Physics and Biology.
Biology and Geology.
Chemistry and Biology.
Physics and Chemistry.
Astronomy and Biology.
explanation_steps: Physical sciences primarily consist of Physics and Chemistry.
Biology and Geology are not the main physical science branches in this context.

subject: Physics
prompt: ML² T⁻¹ is the dimensional formula for
options: Energy.
Linear momentum.
Force.
Pressure.
Angular momentum.
explanation_steps: Angular momentum L = m v r has dimensions M * (L/T) * L = M L² T⁻¹.
Energy is M L² T⁻², linear momentum M L T⁻¹, force M L T⁻², pressure M L⁻¹ T⁻².

subject: Physics
prompt: In some state of matter the molecules are oscillating near their points of equilibrium and cannot move freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?
options: A gas
A solid
A liquid
A fluid
A vapor
explanation_steps: In a solid, molecules vibrate about fixed equilibrium positions and cannot move freely.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of the following has the largest number of significant figures?
explanation_steps: 203 has 3 sig figs; 10.00 has 4; 0.130 has 3; 24.2 has 3; 0.0900 has 3.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which one of the following contains two vector quantities and a scalar quantity?
options: Distance, acceleration, speed.
Displacement, velocity, force.
Distance, mass, speed.
Displacement, velocity, speed.
Mass, time, work.
explanation_steps: Displacement and velocity are vectors; speed is a scalar.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of the following is true about the linear motion of an object with constant velocity?
options: Distance from the initial position is a linear function of time.
Velocity is a linear function of time.
Distance from the initial position is a quadratic function of time.
Acceleration is a non-zero constant.
Acceleration is linear function of time.
explanation_steps: For constant velocity, displacement s = v t, a linear function of time; acceleration is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body starts from rest and acquires a velocity of 10 m/s in 5 s. What are the acceleration of the body and the distance traveled by it during this time interval?
options: 4 m/s², 20 m
2 m/s², 25 m
2 m/s², 40 m
2 m/s², 20 m

subject: Physics
prompt: A freely falling object is dropped from a tower and hits the ground with a speed of 20 m/s. What is the height of the tower in m?

subject: Physics
prompt: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is tangent to the circle.
The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.
The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is directed toward the center of the circle.
The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is perpendicular to its acceleration.
The acceleration of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.
explanation_steps: Velocity is tangential, not directed toward the center (centripetal acceleration is).

subject: Physics
prompt: A motorcar having a mass of 1000 kg accelerates by a net force of 2000 N from rest. What is the speed of the car after 10 seconds (in m/s)?

subject: Physics
prompt: Car A is traveling at 60 km/h due north and another car B is traveling at 70 km/h due south. The velocity of car B relative to A is
options: 10 km/h south.
130 km/h south.
65 km/h north.
10 km/h north.
30 km/h north.
explanation_steps: Relative velocity of B w.r.t. A = v_B - v_A = -70 - 60 = -130 km/h (south).

subject: Physics
prompt: Choose the wrong statement from the following.
options: The total work done on an object is equal to the change in kinetic energy.
The work done on an object is always positive.
The kinetic energy of a moving object is always positive.
When the speed of an object is doubled its kinetic energy quadruples.
Work and energy have the same units.
explanation_steps: Work can be negative (e.g., friction). The others are true.

subject: Physics
prompt: A force of 10 N acts on a 2 kg block (initially at rest) placed on a frictionless horizontal surface for 5 seconds. The change in momentum of the block (in kg·m/s) is

subject: Physics
prompt: Which one of the following is correct for an image formed by a plane mirror?
options: The image is real.
The image is magnified.
The image is inverted.
The image and the object distances from the mirror are always different.
The left hand of the object appears as right hand in the image.
explanation_steps: Plane mirrors produce virtual, erect, same-size images with lateral inversion.

subject: Physics
prompt: If a ray of light goes obliquely from water to air, then the value of the angle of refraction compared to the value of the angle of incidence is:
options: Larger than the angle of incidence.
Always less than the angle of incidence.
Equal to the angle of incidence.
Not related to the angle of incidence.
Less or equal to the angle of incidence.
explanation_steps: From denser (water) to rarer (air) medium, light refracts away from the normal, so angle of refraction > angle of incidence.

subject: Physics
prompt: A spherical convex mirror with an object placed at a distance equal to the radius of curvature (R) from the surface of the mirror produces:
options: A virtual image behind the mirror at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.
A virtual, diminished image behind the mirror at a distance less than the radius of curvature.
A real, magnified image at a distance equal to half of the radius of curvature.
A virtual, magnified image at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.
A real, erect image at a distance equal to half of the radius of curvature.
explanation_steps: For a convex mirror, the image is always virtual, erect, and diminished, located between the focus and the mirror.

subject: Physics
prompt: Secondary colors are colors formed by the combination of various primary colors. Which of the following gives the correct combination?
options: Blue + Red = Magenta
Blue + Green = Yellow
Blue + Yellow = Cyan
Red + Yellow = Green
Green + Red = Cyan
explanation_steps: Primary colors of light: Red + Blue = Magenta; Blue + Green = Cyan; Red + Green = Yellow.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of the following types of forces holds neutrons and protons together in a nucleus?
options: Force of gravitational interaction
Force of electric interaction
Force of magnetic interaction
Force of weak interaction
Force of strong interaction
explanation_steps: The strong nuclear force holds protons and neutrons together in the nucleus.

subject: Physics
prompt: The electrostatic force between two point charges when separated by 10 cm is 1.2 N. What will be the force (in newtons) if they are brought to a separation of 5 cm?
explanation_steps: Coulomb's force F ∝ 1/r². Halving the separation multiplies the force by 4: 1.2 × 4 = 4.8 N.

subject: Physics
prompt: A net charge of 30 C passes through a cross-sectional area of a wire in 2.0 minutes. What is the current in the wire (in amperes)?

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect about heat transfer?
options: Gases are poor conductors of heat.
Metals are good conductors of heat.
Transfer of heat by convection occurs only in fluids.
Heat is transferred from the Sun to the Earth mainly by radiation.
Conduction takes place by mass movement of heated particles.
explanation_steps: Conduction occurs via particle collisions/vibrations without bulk mass movement; mass movement is convection.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which one of the following is correct about an isothermal process?
options: It occurs at constant pressure.
It occurs at constant volume.
It occurs with no heat flow into or out of the system.
It occurs at constant temperature.
It occurs at constant pressure and temperature.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Heat engine is a device that changes thermal energy into mechanical work.
Temperature difference is required to run a heat engine.
A refrigerator takes heat from a high temperature area and releases it to a low temperature area.
Heat does not flow spontaneously from a cold object to a hot object.
Heat flows naturally from a hot object to a cold object.
explanation_steps: A refrigerator extracts heat from a cold region and rejects it to a hotter region (requires work).

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Pressure is the product of force and area.
A pressure of 1 atmosphere is equivalent to 1 newton per square meter.
The standard atmospheric pressure is roughly 760 mm Hg.
A manometer is a device used for measuring atmospheric pressure.
Atmospheric pressure increases as altitude increases.
explanation_steps: Standard atmospheric pressure is approximately 760 mm Hg.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which statement is not true about absolute pressure at a depth h in an open liquid column?
options: The absolute pressure depends on the acceleration due to gravity.
The absolute pressure depends on the liquid’s density.
The absolute pressure is independent of the shape of liquid’s container.
The absolute pressure is independent of the atmospheric pressure on top of the column.
The absolute pressure is independent of the area of the container.
explanation_steps: Absolute pressure P = P_atm + ρgh, so it depends on atmospheric pressure.

subject: Physics
prompt: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: A body sinks in a liquid if its weight is more than the weight of the displaced liquid.
A body rises in a liquid if its weight is less than the weight of the displaced liquid.
A body sinks in a liquid if the buoyant force is more than the weight of the body.
A body floats in a liquid if its weight is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid.
The apparent weight of a body floating in a liquid is zero.
explanation_steps: If buoyant force > weight, the body rises; it sinks when weight > buoyant force.

subject: Physics
prompt: A sound wave is passing through a tube where the area of the cross-section is 2 cm² and the intensity of the wave is 4 W/m². What is the area (in cm²) of the cross-section of the tube in that place where the intensity of the same wave is 0.5 W/m²? Assume that there are no energy losses.
explanation_steps: Power is conserved: I₁A₁ = I₂A₂ → 4 × 2 = 0.5 × A₂ → A₂ = 16 cm².

subject: Physics
prompt: The speed of a sound wave is 330 m/s and the wavelength is 330 cm. What is the period of the sound wave in milliseconds?

subject: Physics
prompt: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about waves?
options: In a transverse wave, particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of motion of the wave.
Mechanical waves do not propagate through vacuum.
Sound wave is a transverse wave.
The speed of electromagnetic waves is much greater than that of mechanical waves.
Waves can carry energy from one place to another.
explanation_steps: Sound waves are longitudinal, not transverse.

subject: Physics
prompt: A man standing in front of a high wall hears the echo of his voice after 2 s. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s, his distance to the wall in meters is
explanation_steps: Distance to wall d = (v × t)/2 = (330 × 2)/2 = 330 m.

subject: Physics
prompt: The device which measures the distance to an object by measuring the time required for a radio wave to reach the object and return, is called
options: laser.
sonar.
radar.
ultrasonic scanner.
tomograph.
explanation_steps: Radar uses radio waves to measure distance via round-trip time.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which one of the following statements is correct about electromagnetic waves?
options: All electromagnetic waves are affected by electric and magnetic fields.
All electromagnetic waves propagate as uniform electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other.
All electromagnetic waves cannot be polarized.
All electromagnetic waves propagate through vacuum with speeds proportional to their wavelengths.
Electromagnetic waves can show interference and diffraction.
explanation_steps: Electromagnetic waves exhibit wave properties including interference and diffraction.

subject: Physics
prompt: Line spectra
options: cannot be used to identify elements.
can be produced by low-density monatomic gases and vapour.
can be produced by high-density monatomic gases and vapour.
can be produced by high-density diatomic gases and vapour.
can be produced by high-density polyatomic gases and vapour.
explanation_steps: Emission line spectra are produced by low-density monatomic gases/vapors.
